description: Expand an agent-cortex pipeline bead into its stage chores, then let the caller reparent them onto the feature bead.

feature.description: Bead ID the stage chores are expanded for; substituted into every chore title.

steps.title: [{{feature}}] Code
steps.description: Implement the task using a test-driven approach.

steps.title: [{{feature}}] Verify
steps.description: Run the project's test and lint commands and report the outcome.

steps.title: [{{feature}}] Review
steps.description: Review the implementation for security, correctness, and alignment with task requirements.

steps.title: [{{feature}}] Document
steps.description: Review changes and update documentation if key decisions, behaviour changes, or constraints were introduced.

steps.title: [{{feature}}] Post-merge check
steps.description: Run `node <ralph-scripts>/post-merge-check.mjs` from the main checkout. It reads `gh run list` for the base branch's merge commit and exits 0 when every run passed, 1 when a run failed, and 2 when the result is inconclusive. Exit 0: report the run URLs and close. Exit 1: the script has already filed one P1 escalation bead carrying the run URL and the failing job — report its id, leave this chore open, and close nothing else. Exit 2: report the reason it printed and leave this chore open. Never retry, never re-run the workflow, never reopen the parent.

steps.title: [{{feature}}] Housekeeping
steps.description: Remove the worktrees of closed beads. Run `node <ralph-scripts>/prune-worktrees.mjs` from the main checkout and retry once if it exits non-zero. Pass `--base origin/epic/<epic-id>` after `git fetch origin` for a feature of a multi-feature epic, and no `--base` otherwise: the stage playbook states how the bead graph tells the two cases apart. The exit status is 1 whenever any worktree survives — an open bead counts as survival — so fail this chore only when a closed-bead worktree is still refused after the retry, and leave it open. Never close it over a worktree the script did not remove.
